name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,577

clue.text: Friend round to study has everything prepared

definitions.note: a phrase meaning 'is all set'; the answer is the adjective phrase it describes

indicators.note: the friend goes round, enclosing the word for study

blocks.note: an ally is a friend
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: A friend comes round to the study and finds everything laid out ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely set to go means every item is prepared beforehand, which is what the phrase conveys.

clue.text: Cunning black rat traps one primate

indicators.note: the rat traps, holding the word for one inside it

blocks.note: arch means slyly knowing
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the Roman numeral for one
to rat on someone is to shop them, British slang for informing on

explanation.surface: A sly black rat captures a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' wants to be an ape; here it is the church title, the chief bishop of a province.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage a primate is the senior bishop of a country, so an archbishop qualifies.

clue.text: Disease beginning to spread, harmless in seaweed

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
in places the preceding letters inside the word for seaweed

blocks.note: the first letter of spread
safe means not dangerous
laver is an edible seaweed

explanation.surface: An illness starts to spread, though harmless when contained in seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic illness first identified in Nigeria, a disease by name.

clue.text: Snake in alien surroundings — through water it sped

indicators.note: the alien forms the surroundings, closing round the snake

blocks.note: ET is the alien from the Spielberg film
a boa is a constrictor snake

explanation.surface: A snake slithers into a strange habitat and speeds off through the water.
explanation.definitionFit: German fast motor torpedo boats of the Second World War raced across the sea at high speed.

clue.text: Covering on the floor is carpeting

blocks.note: a dressing covers a wound
down means on or towards the ground

explanation.surface: A rug laid on the floor is described as carpeting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, to carpet someone is to reprimand them, so carpeting is a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding from a superior is both a carpeting and a reprimand of this sort.

clue.text: Uproar where old woman needs heart transplant

indicators.note: a transplant swaps out the heart, so the two central letters of the old woman change places

blocks.note: beldam is an archaic word for an old woman, often a hag

explanation.surface: Chaos in the hospital as an elderly woman awaits a heart transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle pair of letters in BELDAM is rearranged, turning it into BEDLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after a notorious London asylum, now means a scene of noisy confusion and chaos.

clue.text: Balance in supply provided by French banker

blocks.note: to equip is to supply with gear
a banker is a river, having banks; the Oise is a river in France

explanation.surface: A French banker provides funds to keep the books balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is a state of equal weight or counterpoise between forces, an even balance.

clue.text: Blocks stars in group drinking gallons

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so the star group holds the gallons

blocks.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Celebrities in a band block their path by drinking gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the famous toy brand of interlocking plastic bricks, building blocks for children.

clue.text: Horse and English sheep turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A horse and an English sheep have been brought up on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is an adult female horse, so it is a specific kind of the animal.

clue.text: Character in scrum with toe crushed

indicators.note: something crushed is mangled out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby player in the scrum gets a toe trodden on.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum is the rugby huddle where the forwards push against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal speech an odd or awkward person is 'a queer customer', so customer can mean a character.

clue.text: Great desire suspended by monarch

indicators.note: by means next to, so the monarch is placed alongside the word for suspended

blocks.note: hung means suspended, hanging from something
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A strong wish, left hanging by order of the king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger is used figuratively for any strong craving or longing, not only for food.

clue.text: Books we sent out with positive response time after time

indicators.note: out suggests being sent off in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
amen is a response of agreement, 'so be it'
T again for time

explanation.surface: We posted the books and received a favourable reply again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The response sits between two time signals: one T before it and one after.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament is the collection of Christian scriptures, a set of books of the Bible.

clue.text: Beast's loved one strips, turning to bed early for this

definitions.note: the answer is what one goes to bed early for

indicators.note: turning round means the word for strips is read backwards

blocks.note: in the fairy tale Beauty and the Beast, the Beast loves Beauty
to peel is to strip off

explanation.surface: The Beast's beloved undresses and turns in for an early night.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep taken before midnight is jokingly held to keep one looking attractive, hence the phrase.

clue.text: Missile-launcher that gets the pulse going

definitions.text: Missile-launcher that gets the pulse going

blocks.clueFragment: Missile-launcher that gets the pulse going
blocks.note: surface reading: an exciting weapon that sets the heart racing
setter's reading: pulses are legumes, so this toy fires dried legumes

explanation.walkthrough: Pulse here means edible seeds of legumes, not the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's tube toy for blowing small legume seeds at targets fits a launcher of pulses.

clue.text: Swimmer in famous commercial battle

indicators.note: in places the swimmer inside the following words

blocks.note: star as an adjective means celebrated
an ad is a television commercial
the ling is a fish

explanation.surface: A famous swimmer appears in a television advert about a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The siege of Stalingrad, 1942 to 1943, was a decisive Soviet victory and a famous Second World War battle.

clue.text: Small animals we love reversed dance moves

indicators.note: reversed tells us the whole string so far is read from the end backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
pets are animals kept for affection

explanation.surface: Our beloved little pets have turned around in a dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: In dancing, a step is an individual movement or sequence of foot movements.

clue.text: Mark employed in developing master plan

indicators.note: something developing changes its form, so these letters reshape
being employed in something means working inside it, so the mark goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
a tag is a label or mark

explanation.surface: Mark is hired to help draw up a master plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master plan' reads as one phrase, but master is anagram fodder and plan alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme devised to outwit an opponent, a kind of plan.

clue.text: It sustains teachers with old poetry books

blocks.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Teachers keep themselves going with a diet of classic verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, the food that keeps a living thing alive and growing.

clue.text: Countermands orders I've circulated

indicators.note: something circulated is sent round and round, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss cancels the instructions that were sent round earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: To override an instruction is to cancel or set it aside using higher authority, as countermanding does.

clue.text: One as eligible keeps artistic support

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the letters held within it, spanning its words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of one through as into the start of eligible

explanation.surface: Someone who qualifies is entitled to claim financial support for the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden stand that holds a painter's canvas upright while they work.

clue.text: Those up with the locals?

blocks.note: surface reading: people who are awake, or in the know, alongside the residents
setter's reading: those 'up' at university, in academic gowns, together with the townspeople

explanation.walkthrough: To be 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge is to be in residence as a student; students once wore gowns.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the two communities of a university city: students and staff versus the non-academic residents.

clue.text: Cloth one wraps around copper piping inside

indicators.note: wrapping round something brings one to its far side, so one ends up after copper
inside places piping within the pair of letters already formed

blocks.note: a copper is a penny coin, and d was the old British abbreviation for a penny
piping hot means very hot
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plumber wraps cloth round copper pipe with hot water inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a long loincloth worn by men in India, a garment made from a single cloth.

clue.text: State secrets?

blocks.note: surface reading: classified information held by a government
setter's reading: state as a verb, to tell secrets you should keep

explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a noun for a nation; it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab is to reveal confidential information indiscreetly, carelessly letting out what should stay hidden.

clue.text: Victor perhaps in embrace when given Oscar

blocks.note: a hug is an embrace
Oscar is the NATO alphabet code word for O

explanation.surface: A winner gets a hug when handed an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a winner at the Oscars; it is the first name of the French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo wrote Les Misérables; 'perhaps' signals Victor is one example of someone so surnamed.

clue.text: Dive forward to catch duck in passenger area

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so the dive encloses the duck

blocks.note: to lunge is to make a sudden forward thrust
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A passenger dives forward to catch a duck in the waiting area.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports and stations have a departure lounge, a seating room where travellers wait.

clue.text: One writes news about beer

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A journalist files a story about beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes up news stories for publication.

clue.text: Ulysses hero initially shy comes out

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of James Joyce's novel Ulysses
the opening letter of shy

explanation.surface: Joyce's protagonist, at first bashful, eventually comes out of his shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower blooms when it opens, so blooms and comes out are synonyms for flowering.

clue.text: Fixture on flight seeming to come down in heavy rain?

definitions.text: seeming to come down in heavy rain?

blocks.note: first meaning: a metal bar holding a carpet in place on a flight of stairs

blocks.clueFragment: seeming to come down in heavy rain?
blocks.note: second meaning: in a downpour the British say it is raining ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares straight, heavy rain to the metal bars clamping a carpet to each tread.
